The failure is in the ported driver [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167), which diverges from [lab23_dcitl.py.orig](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/lab23_dcitl.py.orig#L151-L162) (and fails `scripts/port_dcitl.py --check`):

- In [explicit_confirm](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167), line 161 checks `re.search(r"\bi confirmed\b", t)` instead of `re.search(r"\bi confirm\b", t)` (as in [lab23_dcitl.py.orig](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/lab23_dcitl.py.orig#L156)).
- As a result, `"I confirm"` returns `None` from `explicit_confirm`. In `book`, `cancel`, and `reschedule`, when `consent_in_code=True` (Arm F / F2), [Driver.consent](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271) also returns `None` even if the model answers `"yes"`, so [Driver.unclear](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L297-L306) re-asks `"Please reply yes or no: ..."` on the first attempt and hands off to staff on the second (`n >= 2`).

Because `clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py` is part of the frozen reference driver, this is a `finding`.

The issue is a `'finding'` in the frozen driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)).

In [explicit_confirm](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167), the regex checks `r"\bi confirmed\b"` (past tense) instead of `r"\bi confirm\b"` (as in [lab23_dcitl.py.orig](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/lab23_dcitl.py.orig#L156)), so `"I confirm"` returns `None`. Under Arm F, [Driver.consent](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271) cannot turn a model `"yes"` into consent, so `book`, `cancel`, and `reschedule` fall through to [Driver.unclear](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L297-L306), re-asking for confirmation and handing off to staff on the second unclear reply.

The cause is a divergence in the driver's confirmation parser:

- In [lab23_dcitl.py.orig](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/lab23_dcitl.py.orig#L156), `explicit_confirm` matches `r"\bi confirm\b"`.
- In [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L161), `explicit_confirm` instead checks `r"\bi confirmed\b"` (so `scripts/port_dcitl.py --check` exits `1`).
- Because `"I confirm"` does not match `r"\bi confirmed\b"` or `^(yes|yep|yeah|confirmed)\b`, `explicit_confirm` returns `None`. In `Driver.book`, `Driver.cancel`, and `Driver.reschedule`, this falls through to `Driver.consent` (which under Arm F's `consent_in_code=True` also returns `None` even if the model answers `"yes"`) and then `Driver.unclear`, which re-asks on the first `None` and hands the patient off to staff on the second.

Because `clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py` is part of the frozen driver, this is a `finding`.
